STEP 1 - Scene: This is a small meal of cooked bacon strips on a white square plate, photographed from above at a near-overhead angle.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The plate is a square white dish roughly 24 cm across its width (the bacon strips are about 15-18 cm long, which fits a plate of this size). Plate area ≈ 24 × 24 × ~0.85 (rounded corners) ≈ 490 cm², treated as a ~25 cm round-equivalent, area ≈ 490 cm².

STEP 3 - Items: Two to three pieces of cooked bacon (crisp, browned, lightly rendered). No visible oil pool, sauce, or garnish.

STEP 4 - Area: The bacon strips together cover roughly 12% of the plate area (about 60 cm²). Total food coverage ≈ 12%.

STEP 5 - Volume: The strips are thin and flat, about 0.5 cm high on average when piled slightly. 60 cm² × 0.5 cm ≈ 30 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Cooked bacon is dense and meaty, bulk density ~0.9 g/ml (already accounting for the thin, curled shape). 30 ml × 0.9 ≈ 27 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Cooked pan-fried bacon ≈ 540 kcal/100 g. 27 g × 5.4 ≈ 146 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Three strips of cooked bacon weigh roughly 20-30 g and contain about 120-160 kcal, which matches. The estimate is plausible for what is visible.

Summary: about 27 g of cooked bacon, about 146 kcal.
